question: Can official USGS source-page, metadata, and attachment-description evidence determine whether July 14 or July 19, 2017 is the event/recording date?

date_fields.evidence: The USGS page displays 'By Office of Communications July 14, 2017'. This is a page byline/publication date; it is not evidence that the footage was recorded or that the flow occurred on that date.

The same page's Detailed Description explicitly states that the debris flow took place July 19, 2017. This is the publisher's explicit event-date assertion, but it conflicts with the page's earlier byline date and the date reported in the catalog as visible in-frame.

date_fields.field: in-frame date reported by existing project catalog
date_fields.evidence: catalog.csv records 'in-frame 07-14 / official page 07-19 unresolved'. This review did not independently re-inspect frames, and treats the catalog entry as an existing observation, not a newly verified date.
The source download filename and source_id include 2017-07-19. They preserve the original cataloging convention but are not independent evidence of capture or event date.

A HEAD request to the exact download URL returned this HTTP Last-Modified value. It describes the hosted object modification time, not the 2017 filming or event date. The response supplied no capture-date metadata.

sources.support_scope: Page title and byline date; detailed description's explicit event date; stated single view and larger zoomed view; public-domain usage statement.

sources.interpretation_limit: The page gives a page/byline date earlier than the event date asserted in its own description. It does not explain the discrepancy or establish when the camera footage was recorded.

sources.support_scope: Confirms the currently hosted object's HTTP metadata and matching attachment size; provides no 2017 capture, recording, or event date.
sources.interpretation_limit: Last-Modified and multipart ETag are object-storage properties and cannot establish filming or event identity. No media body was downloaded during this review.

safe_grouping_recommendation.same_source_segments: Keep PART01 and PART02 grouped under their shared source/download identity and retain their editorial split as a within-source segmentation. Do not count them as separate events.
safe_grouping_recommendation.date_handling: Keep July 14 and July 19 as distinct provenance fields with their evidence roles. Leave event_date_unverified; do not silently replace the current provisional source key with either date.
safe_grouping_recommendation.independence: Treat this as one unresolved source-event candidate for split planning. Do not assert that it is a newly confirmed independent event, and do not merge it with another event solely because the site or date is similar.
safe_grouping_recommendation.test_use: Keep it outside development/model-based selection. If used in a final external test, report its date identity as unresolved and preserve both segments in one group.

scope_notes: No model predictions or scores were read.
No new media was searched for or downloaded; no AutoDL access was made.
The attachment page's video link could not be rendered by the web reader because it is video/mp4; an HTTP HEAD request was used only to inspect response metadata.
